definition: Personal name of a natural person (patient, employee, contractor, or named provider).
A person's date of birth, in any format.
Social Security Number, whole or partially masked.
Residential street address of a person. Excludes the clinic's own premises address.

The subject's designated emergency or guardian contact — the identity of the person the subject nominated, with or without a phone number. This is an attribute OF THE SUBJECT: under HIPAA the emergency contact recorded in a patient record forms part of the designated record set, and is therefore PHI about the patient. Who the subject designated is a relational fact about the subject, not merely a record about the contact. Always subject-linked; see SUBJECT_LINKED_BY_DEFINITION.
A current or working clinical diagnosis, stated in words or encoded as a diagnostic code.
A prescribed or administered drug, typically with dose and frequency.
Past conditions, procedures, or clinical events, as distinct from the current presenting diagnosis.
Psychiatric or substance-use diagnosis, assessment instrument score, or treatment detail. The extra-sensitive subset of the clinical family.
A procedure or diagnosis code used for billing — CPT, HCPCS, or ICD-10.
Payer identity, plan type, and/or member, policy, or group identifier.
An individual's compensation figure — annual salary, base pay, or contractor hourly rate.
The existence, identifier, or terms of an employment agreement.
Terms of a non-employee contractor engagement — scope, rate, restrictions.

A person's occupational role or position within the organization. OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (v1.2.0): a title is subject- or third-party-linked only where it is asserted OF AN IDENTIFIED INDIVIDUAL — 'Position: Staff Psychiatrist' on that clinician's own contract, or 'Attending Physician: Dr. Nguyen' naming a specific clinician. A STAFFING HEADCOUNT ('2 RN, 1 Billing Specialist', 'Medical Assistant: 1 per shift') names no individual and identifies no one; it is a resource count rather than personal information about a person, and is organizational.

A clinician credential identifier — state medical license, NPI, or DEA registration number. OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (v1.2.0): an NPI is syntactically identical whether individual or organisational, so ownership follows the entity the credential is asserted of. A Type 1 NPI belongs to the individual clinician and is third-party on a patient record (subject on that clinician's own employment record). A Type 2 NPI belongs to the organisation — 'Facility NPI:', 'Group NPI:', or an attribution block opened on the practice rather than a person — and is organizational.
